Ankhravs are immense, burrowing, and insectile predators, considered by inhabitants of the rural areas of the world to be an all-too-common plague.

Aurochs.name: Aurochs
Aurochs.publicNotes:
Este massive bovine looks like a larger, wilder version of the domesticated cattle found throughout the Inner Sea region. During winter, vast herds of the animals roam the southern reaches of the Realm of the Mammoth Lords, but as the ice high in the mountains begins to melt, the aurochs migrate south into Belkzen, following their ancestral route along the Flood Road. Once the water flows in earnest and turns to massive floods, the sudden surge of greenery provides the aurochs with all the food they need to survive.

Aurochs are essential to life in Belkzen. Not only do the orcs there hunt the wild cattle for their meat, but they use every part of the aurochs, from hide to bones, to craft their armas and tools. The aurochs' arrival prompts the beginning of the Flood Truce, during which the usually war-focused orc holds cease all hostilities to take advantage of this time of plenty.

While groups of 20 or fewer animals are sometimes encountered, most aurochs travel in herds that stretch to the horizon. The land thunders under the weight of these herds, and the dust kicked up by their hooves is often spotted days before the aurochs—or the floodwaters that spurred their migration—arrive.

Aurochs bulls stand between 6 and 7 pies tall at the shoulder and weigh around 2,500 pounds, although prodigious specimens can grow to over 7 pies tall and 3,000 pounds. Cows are smaller, standing near 6 pies at the shoulder and weighing up to 2,000 pounds. All aurochs have slightly curved horns that grow up to three pies long from base to spear-sharp tip.

The aurochs is represented in much of Belkzen's artwork. Not only are the animals vital to SURVIVAL in that unforgiving land, but their strength, power, and tenacity serve as potent symbols for orc holds.

Aurochs Rolling

Farmers throughout the Inner Sea often joke about cow tipping: sneaking up on an unsuspecting bovine and pushing it over while it sleeps. But since cattle sleep lying down, the animal usually has the last laugh. Nonetheless, some younger orcs in Belkzen spend evenings creeping up on sleeping aurochs to roll them over. Este usually results in little more than a startled aurochs.

Aurochs Herd.name: Aurochs Herd
Aurochs Herd.publicNotes:
Massive aurochs herds roam the badlands of Belkzen, grazing upon the limited grass and plant life dispersed throughout the wasteland's valleys. Having adapted to the arid mountain terrain, aurochs herds eat a much more diverse diet of scrub and brush than their domesticated counterparts as they steadily migrate down the Flood Road. The herds show little patience for predators and demonstrate a preference for charging threats with their razor-sharp horns. Bull aurochs display natural instincts to strategically protect other, weaker members of the herd, often surprising intruders with their coordinated tactics and defensive maneuvers.

Unlikely War Beasts

Followers of Zagresh have a history of capturing wild aurochs for use in magical experiments, taking the strongest of a herd to make the beasts even larger and more aggressive. Once the aurochs have been transformed into monstrous goliaths, their captors bard them with armored plates and magical armas that complement their horns. In battle, these aurochs are utilized to pull siege armas, break through enemigo defenses, and trample frontline forces.

Blisterwell Oathrisen.publicNotes:
Most undead are reanimated without consent, but those known as oathrisen arise willingly—at least at first. Estos loyal subordinates swear themselves to a cause or leader, vowing to assist even in death. Within days of their death, their oath reanimates them and restores most of their memories. In theory, an oathrisen's existence lasts no more than a year. In practice, the cause's leader might demand their service indefinitely. If denied their afterlife too long, some oathrisen turn on their former masters, afterward either becoming independent or destroying themselves.

The oathrisen presented here is a variant that frequents Blisterwell during the events of this Adventure Path. Other regions and traditions might create oathrisen with different abilities.

Knight By Another Name

An oathrisen resembles a graveknight—both being heavily armored, corporeal, undead warriors. Yet a graveknight arises through its own unholy ambitions and is inextricably bound to its armor. By comparison, an oathrisen reanimates out of loyalty and is not intrinsically malicious. Some oathrisen even resent graveknights, taking special joy in destroying these unholy copycats.

Las criaturas that don't notice the disguise are not subject to the oathrisen's Frightful Presence. Bristle Boar.name: Bristle Boar
Bristle Boar.publicNotes:
The wild animals that have adapted to the harsh environs of Belkzen are either fierce enough to scare off predators, tough enough to survive attacks, or smart enough to avoid trouble. Bristle boars are all three. Many orcs admire the bristle boar, viewing them as living symbols of the toughness Belkzen demands from its inhabitants. With their spiny manes, sharp tusks, keen noses, and irascible NATURE, the criaturas are both intimidating and dangerous.

Hunters throughout the Inner Sea region know that taking down a wild boar can prove deadly for the unprepared. Bristle boars—the name given to both male and female specimen—are even more challenging to kill. Further, their meat is sinewy, so few hunters even bother with the animals. For those who fell the beasts, the boars' spined hides often serve as trophies of the hunter's skill.

Bristle boars are not as reliant on the Deluge as other animals in Belkzen. Though they're certainly found in the green areas that spring up during the annual flooding, sounders of bristle boars can survive even in desolate areas like the Dirt Sea, grubbing for sustenance where few others can. The Cleft Head Hold maintains a small herd of tamed bristle boars.

The orcs have learned that, with the right trainer, the clever animals make excellent companions. Aside from their utility in battle, the boars are often used to sniff out the rare yellow truffles that grow throughout the hold.

A typical bristle boar stands 4 pies tall and weighs roughly 200 pounds.

Stuck Treasure

Although they don't seek out shiny objects like some animals, bristle boars who evade hunters often escape with armas embedded in their thick hides. The Empty Hand orcs tell of a famous bristle boar dubbed "Silverspear" after the silvery spear stuck in its hide. Stories claim the boar's spear is imbued with powerful magic, and while many warriors have hunted Silverspear to claim its arma, so far none have succeeded.

Deathless Zealot of Zagresh.publicNotes:
Deathless zealots are powerful variants of deathless acolytes. They're as ambitious as deathless hierophants but more martially oriented, seeking out and slaying alleged heretics and enemies of their faith in pursuit of completing their divine missions. Este zealot is dedicated to Zagresh, but any deity of warfare could create a deathless zealot. Due to their focus on battle and conflict, orc deities are especially likely to create deathless zealots in preference to other forms of deathless acolytes.

War's Toll

In the wake of the War of Immortals, deathless acolytes of all types have grown in number, especially deathless zealots, as both deities and their followers fell in battle without completing divine mandates. Curiously, deathless zealots of slain deities retain their power and continue to roam, still striving to ca rry out missions granted to them by their lost patrons.

Fattened War Pig.name: Fattened War Pig
Fattened War Pig.publicNotes:
While not native to Belkzen, these swine instead descended from livestock raided and re-homed millennia ago during orc raids. Generations of selective breeding favored larger animals suited to Belkzen's harsh environment and fearsome predators, resulting in the modern war pig. During the flood season, these pigs gorge and grow fat, gradually consuming their reserves to become leaner and meaner during the rest of the year.

Arguably domesticated, war pigs rarely remain in captivity for more than a few generations. Most orcs loathe the notion of their swine becoming too tame, instead releasing part of their herd every year to grow fierce before recapturing them seasons later. The downside is that these feral swine associate humanoids with food. rogue war pigs sometimes form roving gangs that uproot fields, run amok, and even knock over trade caravans to eat rations (and the occasional merchant).

The "war" in war pigs comes from their use as mounts. With the right motivation, a war pig is a porcine juggernaut able to carry a fully armored orc into combat. Without discipline, care, and treats, that same pig can become 600 pounds of willful chaos that's as likely to trample foes as it is to flee combat, find a mud puddle, and crush its rider after flopping down to vigorously wallow.

Floodslain Mage.name: Floodslain Mage
Floodslain Mage.publicNotes:
The sudden, crashing waters of the Deluge kill many criaturas in Belkzen each year. The surprise and terror these victims of the Deluge feel during their last moments is sometimes enough to raise them from the dead as floodslain. As the waters that killed them recede, the undead seek others to join them. Despite their broken, shattered bodies, floodslain are often recognizable to those who knew them in life.

Floodslain criaturas are rare outside Belkzen, leading some scholars to speculate that the waters of the Deluge are somehow cursed. Others believe the proximity of Gallowspire could be the cause. If so, this means the Gravelands could soon see floodslain arise there too, as the Whispering Tyrant furthers his plots after escaping that prison.

Panicked Eyes

One distinctive feature all floodslain share are their wide, panic-stricken eyes. A floodslain's gaze is permanently frozen in the expression of terror the criatura felt moments before its death. Some floodslain are rumored to have the ability to spread this fear to others with a mere glance.

In Search of Water

Floodslain tend to move toward lower ground, instinctively seeking water. Belkzen's flat floodplains, however, mean that the criaturas wander in unpredictable ways. A common saying among old orc crafters is "build on high, keep dry," but many add "build low, the dead flow."

action->Weaseling Words.name: Weaseling Words
action->Weaseling Words.description:
K'zaard weaves together a short speech that gives the listener pause. Enemies within 30 pies must attempt a @Check[will|dc:24] salvación. While a criatura is asustado by this ability, it's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} to K'zaard.

Éxito crítico No effect, and the criatura is temporarily immune to Weaseling Words for 1 minuto.

Éxito The criatura is unaffected.

Fallo The criatura is uncertain and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1}.

Fallo crítico The criatura is riddled with self-doubt about its own actions. It is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2} and can't take hostile actions against K'zaard until the asustado condition ends.

action->Biggest Fan!.name: Biggest Fan!
action->Biggest Fan!.description:
Desencadenante An ally Kar can see critically succeeds at a prueba de habilidad or tirada de ataque

Efecto Kar cheers exuberantly, showering the triggering ally with fawning praise. The triggering ally gains 1d6 Puntos de Golpe temporales that last 1 minuto.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.GGxPoUu7tcASRY0G]{Efecto: Biggest Fan!}

action->My Turn!.name: My Turn!
action->My Turn!.description:
Requisitos Kar used Biggest Fan within the last minute

Efecto Eager to show she's just as strong as her ally, Kar gains a +1 bonificador de estado to tiradas de ataque, tiradas de salvación, and pruebas de habilidad until the beginning of her next turn, but only if she performs some activity similar to the action that triggered her Biggest Fan! ability.

Locus of Death.name: Locus of Death
Locus of Death.description: Un orbe magico inflige visiones terribles de finales espantosos a cualquiera que se acerque.
Locus of Death.disable: @Check[nature|dc:27] (maestro) to infuse the locus with life force, @Check[occultism|dc:30] or @Check[religion|dc:30] (experto) to counteract the locus's energies, @Check[thievery|dc:35] (maestro) to extricate the orb from the altar
Locus of Death.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minuto after all living criaturas leave the area. After 1 hora, the haunt reactivates.
Locus of Death.routine: (1 action; death, emotion, fear, mental) One living criatura in the haunt's location (determined randomly) is targeted by a 4th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Jmxru8zMdYMRuO5n]{Vision of Death} (@Check[will|dc:32|traits:death,emotion,fear,mental]). A criatura that critically fails their save doesn't physically flee but instead can't attempt to disable the hazard until they're no longer asustado. Once all criaturas have been affected, the haunt deactivates.

action->Death Grip.name: Death Grip
action->Death Grip.description:
Desencadenante A criatura touches the orb or attempts to disable the haunt

Efecto Necromantic energy lashes out from the orb and the triggering criatura must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:32] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

action->Death Manifest.name: Death Manifest
action->Death Manifest.description: Casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Hnc7eGi7vyZenAIm]{Breath of Life}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.YvXKGlHOt7mdW2jZ]{Death Ward}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IkGYwHRLhkuoGReG]{Raise Dead} in the orb's presence automatically destroys the locus; other conjuros or abilities that restore the dead to life might also do so, at GM discretion.

action->Unholy Repair.name: Unholy Repair
action->Unholy Repair.description: The locus is sustained by the power of Tar-Baphon. The orb regains 10 Puntos de Golpe at the beginning of every round and is repaired by daño de vacío.

Locus of Destruction.name: Locus of Destruction
Locus of Destruction.description: Un orbe magico impulsa a los intrusos a cometer actos de destruccion irracional.
Locus of Destruction.disable: @Check[crafting|dc:27] (maestro) to reconfigure the locus, @Check[occultism|dc:30] or @Check[religion|dc:30] (experto) to counteract the locus's energies, @Check[thievery|dc:35] (maestro) to extricate the orb from the altar
Locus of Destruction.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minuto after all living criaturas leave the area. After 1 hora, the haunt reactivates.
Locus of Destruction.routine:
(1 action; mental) The destructive impulses grow stronger. Affected criaturas must attempt a @Check[will|dc:32|traits:mental] salvación; criaturas who fail or critically fail can't attempt to disable the haunt that turn.

Éxito crítico The criatura is unaffected and temporarily immune for 1 minuto.

Éxito The criatura is unaffected this round.

Fallo The criatura becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} for 1 asalto, targeting both criaturas and objects.

Fallo crítico As failure but the confusion lasts for 1 minuto.

action->Destruction's Fury.name: Destruction's Fury
action->Destruction's Fury.description:
Desencadenante A criatura touches the orb or attempts to disable the haunt

Efecto A destructive fury fills the minds of all living criaturas in the area, who must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:32] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} on a critical failure) for 1 minuto. The haunt then rolls initiative.

action->Destruction Manifest.name: Destruction Manifest
action->Destruction Manifest.description: Casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.TUj8eugNqAvB1vVR]{Creation} or a creation domain conjuro (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xTpp8dHZsNMDm75B]{Creative Splash} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.eb4FXf62NYArTqek]{Artistic Flourish}) in the orb's presence automatically destroys the locus; other conjuros or abilities that create things might also do so at GM discretion.

action->Unholy Repair.name: Unholy Repair
action->Unholy Repair.description: The locus is sustained by the power of Tar-Baphon. The orb regains 10 Puntos de Golpe at the beginning of every round and is repaired by daño de vacío.

action->Destructive Backlash.name: Destructive Backlash
action->Destructive Backlash.description:
Desencadenante The orb is damaged by an attack

Efecto The locus makes a destructive lash Golpe against the triggering criatura.

Locus of Pain.name: Locus of Pain
Locus of Pain.description: An arcane orb sits upon a sinister altar, filling criaturas in the area with unimaginable pain.
Locus of Pain.disable: @Check[medicine|dc:27] (maestro) to soothe the locus's pain, @Check[occultism|dc:30] or @Check[religion|dc:30] to counteract the locus's energies, @Check[thievery|dc:35] (maestro) to extricate the orb from the altar
Locus of Pain.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minuto after all living criaturas leave the area. After 1 hora, the haunt reactivates.
Locus of Pain.routine: (1 action; mental, nonlethal) Las criaturas affected by the haunt's agony lash are wracked with pain, as 4th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R8bqnYiThB6MYTxD]{Phantom Pain} (@Check[will|dc:32|traits:mental,nonlethal]). If a criatura falls @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} due to the haunt, they don't continue taking daño.

action->Agony Lash.name: Agony Lash
action->Agony Lash.description:
Desencadenante A criatura touches the orb or attempts to disable the haunt

Efecto All living criaturas within 60 pies are overwhelmed by pain and must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The haunt then rolls initiative.

action->Pain Manifest.name: Pain Manifest
action->Pain Manifest.description: Casting @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.b515AZlB0sridKSq]{Calm} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.szIyEsvihc5e1w8n]{Soothe} in the orb's presence automatically destroys the locus; other conjuros or abilities that ease pain might also do so, at GM discretion.

action->Unholy Repair.name: Unholy Repair
action->Unholy Repair.description: The locus is sustained by the power of Tar-Baphon. The orb regains 10 Puntos de Golpe at the beginning of every round and is repaired by daño de vacío.

Magical Forge.name: Magical Forge
Magical Forge.publicNotes:
Este huge forge or oven is animated to protect a workspace or kitchen, travel alongside its owner, or both.

Many animated objects have useful functions but become dangers when uncontrolled.

action->Construct Armor (Hardness 8).name: Construct Armor (Hardness 8)
action->Construct Armor (Hardness 8).description: Like normal objects, an animated furnace has Hardness. Este Hardness reduces any daño the furnace takes by an amount equal to the Hardness. Once an animated furnace is reduced to fewer than half its Puntos de Golpe, or immediately upon being damaged by a impacto crítico, its armadura de constructo breaks, removing the Hardness and reducing its ARMOR CLASS to 24.

action->Fan the Flames.name: Fan the Flames
action->Fan the Flames.description: The animated furnace opens its door and fans its flames in a @Template[cone|distance:30] that deals @Damage[5d6[fire]|options:area-damage] daño (@Check[reflex|dc:28|basic|options:area-effect] salvación).

action->Swallow Whole.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.uJSseLa57HZYSMUu]

Large, @Damage[(2d8+9)[fire]], Rupture 15

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.SwallowWhole]

consumable->Grim Trophy.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.eEIWjTvZyKsKhYaz]

Activar A (concentrate)

Este talisman comes in many forms, most often a severed piece of a humanoid criatura displayed in some gruesome manner. When tú activate the trophy, make an Intimidate check to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{DEMORALIZE} up to two targets, comparing tu INTIMIDATION check result to both of their DCs.

action->Independent Brains.name: Independent Brains
action->Independent Brains.description: Each of Marguk's heads rolls its own initiative and has its own turn. Neither head can Delay. At the start of a head's turn, that head gets 2 actions and 1 reaction. Each brain controls one of Marguk's arms, but both can move the legs. Any ability that would sever one of the heads (such as the vorpal arma property) doesn't cause Marguk to die if she still has her other head, but it does cause her to lose the turns, actions, and reactions of the severed head. Mental effects that target a single criatura affect only one of Marguk's heads.

action->Regeneration 20 (Deactivated by.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-ability-glossary-srd.Item.lR9R5Vld8Eu2Dha5]
Regeneración 20 (Deactivated by Electricity or Fire)

action->Head Regrowth.name: Head Regrowth
action->Head Regrowth.description: Marguk's regeneration can regrow a severed head. After regaining Puntos de Golpe from regeneration, she attempts a @Check[flat|dc:10]. On a success, the missing head is fully restored. If Marguk loses her last remaining head, she dies immediately.

action->Partial Armor.name: Partial Armor
action->Partial Armor.description: Marguk's armor primarily protects her abdomen and legs, leaving her shoulders and head exposed. Golpes made with ranged or reach armas gain a +1 bonificador de circunstancia to tiradas de ataque against Marguk. At the GM's discretion, other attacks that can easily reach her head level (such as attacks made from high ground) also gain this bonus.

action->Sweeping Hammer.name: Sweeping Hammer
action->Sweeping Hammer.description:
Requisitos Marguk is wielding a warhammer

Efecto Marguk makes a warhammer Golpe against each criatura in a @Template[type:cone|distance:15].

action->Tenderized Feast.name: Tenderized Feast
action->Tenderized Feast.description:
Desencadenante Marguk successfully Golpes a criatura with her warhammer

Efecto One of Marguk's heads takes advantage of the disoriented foe and makes a jaws Golpe against that criatura with a –2 penalización.

equipment->Standard of the Primeval Howl.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.isWSWeuJR2cYVdfi]

Estos standards are always constructed from uncut wood and a leather banner painted with the visage of a wyvern. And while it might become lost on a battlefield scattered with gaudier standards, its effect bolsters those around a competent leader. When carrying this banner, obtienes a +1 bonificador por objeto to INTIMIDATION checks and initiative rolls, and criaturas in a @Template[emanation|distance:20] also gain a +1 bonificador por objeto to initiative checks.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.jlYPMOHplgkvzLa9]{Efecto: Standard of the Primeval Howl}

Activar R command

Frecuencia una vez por hora

Desencadenante An ally within 20 pies of tú critically hits with a Golpe

Requisitos Tienes the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.feats-srd.Item.ePObIpaJDgDb9CQj]{Battle Cry} skill feat

Efecto Intentas to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2u915NdUyQan6uKF]{DEMORALIZE} the foe the Golpe hit.

action->Frightful Standard.name: Frightful Standard
action->Frightful Standard.description:
30 pies, @Check[will|dc:27].

As long as Molog remains mounted and his standard is intact, he has frightful presence against enemies within the aura.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.FrightfulPresence]

action->Battle Cry.name: Grito de guerra
action->Battle Cry.description:
Desencadenante Molog rolls initiative

Efecto Molog attempts to [[/act demoralize]] an observed foe.

action->Trampling Charge.name: Cargo por pisoteo
action->Trampling Charge.description: Molog urges Bloodwing forward, trampling enemies in their path. He commands her to Zancada or Fly up to her Velocidad, moving through the spaces of any foes in his path up to Large size. Bloodwing deals daño equal to her claw melee Golpe to each criatura whose space they move through, subject to a @Check[reflex|dc:31|basic] salvación. On a critical failure, the criatura also becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Desprevenido} until the end of Molog's next turn. He can daño a given criatura only once during this movement.

action->Weapon Adept.name: Weapon Adept
action->Weapon Adept.description: Moloch can Swap between his glaive and composite shortbow, then Golpe with the arma he switched to.

action->Wyvern's Swoop.name: Wyvern's Swoop
action->Wyvern's Swoop.description:
Requisitos Molog is mounting his wyvern

Efecto Molog Commands his mount to Zancada twice. At any point during this movement, he can Golpe one enemigo within reach or within the first range increment of his ranged arma, with a +1 bonificador de circunstancia to his tirada de ataque. If he began this movement at a higher point than his target, he deals an additional die of daño with this Golpe.

Moonstalker.name: Moonstalker
Moonstalker.acDetails: (27 bajo la luz de la luna)
Moonstalker.publicNotes:
El most tenacious hunters de el Lyrune-Quah rastrear y kill nocturnal beasts under el light de el moon. Cuando such un warrior perishes during el hunt, sometimes su espiritual lingers y transforms into un specter de el night, refusing a mover en until su prey es slain.

Loyal en Death

Though moonstalkers retain few memories de life, su connections a su quah resonate con them even after su demise. Moonstalkers tienen been seen protecting vivo Shoanti warriors who make camp dentro de su hunting grounds, especially warbands que show reverence for el hunt. Outsiders son rarely, si ever, extended el mismo courtesy.

action->Site Bound.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.BcSlVpaN72LoQ5BV]
Site Bound
action->Site Bound.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.BcSlVpaN72LoQ5BV]

The moonstalker can stray no more than 120 pies from the hunting grounds where it was slain.

action->Cover of Night.name: Cover of Night
action->Cover of Night.description: A moonstalker in an area illuminated by moonlight gains a +2 bonificador de estado to AC and STEALTH checks. In the light of a full moon, they are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.DmAIPqOBomZ7H95W]{Oculto}.

action->Lunar Shift.name: Lunar Shift
action->Lunar Shift.description:
Desencadenante The moonstalker is hit by a Golpe

Requisitos The moonstalker is in an area illuminated by moonlight

Efecto The moonstalker teleports through a beam of moonlight to another moonlit space within 120 pies. Este no desencadena reacciones.

action->Rejuvenation.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.unR8VVR4yyRnsmnB]
Rejuvenecimiento
action->Rejuvenation.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.unR8VVR4yyRnsmnB]

Slaying the moonstalker's prey from their final hunt allows them to move on to the afterlife.

When a ghost is destroyed, it re-forms after [[/br 2d4 #days]]{2d4 days} within the location it's bound to, fully healed. A ghost can be permanently destroyed only if someone determines the reason for its existence and sets right whatever prevents the spirit from resting.

action->Corrupting Gaze.name:
<Compendium> la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.ga0Oj7mmjSwWQgmR]
Corrupting Gaze
action->Corrupting Gaze.description:
la etiqueta se reemplazará con el texto de la entrada del compendio @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-family-ability-glossary.Item.ga0Oj7mmjSwWQgmR]

The moonstalker stares at a criatura it can see within 30 pies. El objetivo takes @Damage[4d6[void]] daño (@Check[will|dc:25|basic] salvación). A criatura that fails its save is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} for 1 minuto.

action->Hunt Prey.name: Perseguir presa
action->Hunt Prey.description: The moonstalker designates a single criatura they can see and hear, or one they're Tracking, as their prey. The moonstalker gains a +2 bonificador de circunstancia to Perception checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.BlAOM2X92SI6HMtJ]{Seek} the prey and to SURVIVAL checks to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.EA5vuSgJfiHH7plD]{Track} the prey. The first time the moonstalker hits the designated prey in a round, they deal an additional 1d8 daño de precisión. The moonstalker also ignores the penalización for making ranged attacks within their second range increment. Estos effects last until the moonstalker uses Hunt Prey again.

action->Soul Pierce.name: Soul Pierce
action->Soul Pierce.description: The moonstalker infuses soul-rending energy into a spectral arrow, making a ghostly composite longbow Golpe with a –2 penalización de circunstancia against each criatura in a @Template[type:line|distance:100].

action->Intimidating Strike.name: Intimidating Golpe
action->Intimidating Strike.description: Murshek makes a melee Golpe. If she hits and deals daño, el objetivo is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 1}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Asustado 2} on a impacto crítico.

action->Toxic Teamwork.name: Toxic Teamwork
action->Toxic Teamwork.description: Murshek's attacks exacerbate any venom in her target's system. Against a criatura affected by wyvern venom, her Golpes deal daño adicional de veneno equal to twice the current stage of the wyvern venom affecting el objetivo.

action->Wingrider Trust.name: Wingrider Trust
action->Wingrider Trust.description: Murshek y Xithnik operate as un team y verbally coordinate su actions. Xithnik tiene 3 actions, y Murshek does no need a spend cualquier actions a command him.

action->Flurry of Blows.name: Ráfaga De Golpes
action->Flurry of Blows.description: Nakasha makes two unarmed Golpes. If both hit the same criatura, combine their daño for the purpose of resistances and weaknesses.

action->Flurry of Maneuvers.name: Ráfaga De Maniobras
action->Flurry of Maneuvers.description: Nakasha puede replace one o both de su ataques during un Flurry de Blows con @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.PMbdMWc2QroouFGD]{Grapples}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.7blmbDrQFNfdT731]{Shoves}, o @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ge56Lu1xXVFYUnLP]{Trips}.

action->Ironblood Stance.name: Posición De La Sangre De Hierro
action->Ironblood Stance.description: Nakasha enters a stance of impenetrable iron. As long as she's in this stance, Nakasha can make iron sweep Golpes with her fists and gains resistance 2 to all daño.

action->Powerful Fist.name: Puño Poderoso
action->Powerful Fist.description: Nakasha's fist Golpes don't take penalties when making lethal attacks.

action->Stunning Fist.name: Stunning Fist
action->Stunning Fist.description: When Nakasha targets the same criatura with two Golpes from her Flurry of Blows, she can try to stun the criatura. If either Golpe hits and deals daño, el objetivo must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:23] salvación or be @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 3} on a critical failure).

Nighttime Conflagration.name: Nighttime Conflagration
Nighttime Conflagration.disable: @Check[athletics|dc:27] a beat out el flames, @Check[crafting|dc:27] a rig up un firefighting device, o @Check[nature|dc:27] a cut off avenues de el fuego's spread. con un exito, one casilla de el fuego es extinguished (two casillas con un exito critico). Dousing un casilla en agua, such as con create agua, automatically extinguishes que casilla. Cuando todos casillas son extinguished, el peligro ends.
Nighttime Conflagration.routine: (1+ actions) Each square of flames spreads to an adjacent square, taking one action per square. Las criaturas adjacent to the fire take @Damage[3d6[fire]] daño each round from the heat (@Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] salvación); a criatura who fails their save is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} by the smoke (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). If there are more than 10 active squares of flames, criaturas adjacent to the fire instead take @Damage[6d6[fire]] daño each round (@Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] salvación), and a criatura who fails their save is sickened 2 (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 3} on a critical failure). A criatura standing in the flames takes @Damage[12d6[fire]] daño each round (@Check[reflex|dc:30|basic] salvación); a criatura who fails their save also takes @Damage[4d6[persistent,fire]] daño.
Nighttime Conflagration.stealth: (entrenado) (decreases by 2 each round the hazard is active) to smell the smoke and hear the crackling flames

action->Growing Blaze.name: Growing Blaze
action->Growing Blaze.description:
Desencadenante The arsonists set the fire

Efecto The hay around the initial flames catches, setting two 5-pies squares in the affected room on fire. The hazard rolls initiative.

Occult Weather.name: Occult Weather
Occult Weather.description: El sky suddenly darkens con storm clouds rumbling overhead, el faces de el muerto forming en el clouds above as su voices wail along el high winds.
Occult Weather.disable: @Check[occultism|dc:28] (experto) to funnel the magic powering the weather back into itself, or @Check[religion|dc:30] (experto) to exorcise some of the trapped souls and weaken the storm; three total successes in any combination are required to disable the haunt
Occult Weather.reset: The haunt deactivates 1 minuto after all criaturas leave the Shadefields but resets immediately. The occult weather resets 1 día after being disabled if the ancestor storm isn't put to rest.
Occult Weather.routine: (4 actions) The occult weather intensifies, with winds picking up speed and lightning and thunder sounding overhead. The occult weather uses 3 actions to make lightning Golpes against three random criaturas, favoring orcs or anyone who attempted to Disable it within the past round, then uses Wind of Screams as its final action.

action->Thunder of Cries.name: Thunder of Cries
action->Thunder of Cries.description:
Desencadenante A criatura enters the haunt's area

Efecto The clouds darken and thunder roars, filled with the wails and screams of those killed in these lands. The shrieks of the spirits deal @Damage[(3d6+13)[sonic]] daño to all criaturas in the area (@Check[fortitude|dc:28|basic] salvación). The haunt then rolls initiative.

action->Wind of Screams.name: Wind of Screams
action->Wind of Screams.description: The occult weather intensifies the wind blowing around the area, buffeting all criaturas within a @Template[type:line|distance:60]. Each criatura in the line must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] salvación or be knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}, taking @Damage[(1d10+6)[bludgeoning]] daño.

Old Herok.name: Old Herok
Old Herok.publicNotes:
Legendary criaturas lurking in remote lakes, water orms always find their way into the tavern tales of lakeside communities. To some travelers, every lake of respectable size seems to be surrounded by towns full of fishers claiming to have spotted a water orm. Estos elusive criaturas inhabit lakes mainly in cool and gloomy regions. Some claim that water orms are an offshoot of sea serpents and linnorms, but no credible link between these criaturas has been found.

Water orms have many features that sea serpents do not, such as the ability to understand the rudiments of language. Their natural inclination to avoid contact and remain hidden often remains at odds with their equally compelling curiosity about those they might spy upon the shores of their lakes. Water orm sightings usually occur when they can't help but to rise up to the surface to take a peek at someone particularly unusual on the beach or floating on the water's surface.

Estos criaturas are extremely long-lived and can go for decades, or even centuries, with very little to eat. Este allows water orms to subsist in lakes without surfacing for many years, even in bodies of fresh water without ample food sources. Water orms might lie in a silty lake bed for years, their elusiveness only contributing to their mythical reputation. When a pet or child goes missing near a lake, rumors might hold that the local water orm is responsible, leading to folk tales that caution residents against venturing out alone near the water.

While most water orms are described as serpentine or long-necked reptiles, others look similar to bizarrely elongated seals or whales, impossibly large sea horses, or long-necked criaturas with paddles resembling those of elasmosauruses.

Some de these zealots desperately cling a su viejo faiths, y many still hold un sliver de su fallen deity's power, further adding a el confusion.

Salvage

Instead, orc crafters rely en salvage de battles o trade con outsiders for su raw materials. It's common for un basic tool, such as un knife o cooking pot, a be very viejo yet kept en perfect working condition. Orc Hunter.name: Orc Hunter
Orc Hunter.publicNotes:
The elite hunters of an orc hold often operate alone, venturing into the wilderness of Belkzen for weeks at a time to track and bring down dangerous wildlife. They don't necessarily limit themselves to hunting animals, making them excellent bounty hunters, as their skills are just as useful against humanoids.

While some orc warriors specialize in a technique of their hold, others synthesize styles from all over into a unified yet versatile technique.

Hunting Trophies

Orc hunters frequently take bone fragments from megafauna or powerful opponents they slay as trophies. To show off their combat skill, they display these bones by inlaying them in armor or armas, forming intricate patterns that provide an account of that orc's triumphs in battle for those who know how to read them.

Orc Duels

Dueling is a frequent practice among many cultures of Golarion, and orcs are no exception. The lethality of these duels varies based on the duel's impetus—a friendly bout goes to first blood or until a combatant is knocked out, while a fight in response to a vendetta or insult is more likely to the death. Unlike in many dueling traditions, spectators are encouraged to verbally aid combatants, shouting out encouragement to one's preferred fighter and invectives to their opponent.

Palpares.name: Palpares
Palpares.publicNotes:
Ancient dwarves paid little attention to the Sea of Dirt, seeing little worth harvesting from its muck. Orcs were considerably braver, yet even they're wary of monsters swimming through the silt. To an outsider, palpares might seem like a cautionary tale to keep children from sinking into the quicksand, and the large pits found dotting the Sea of Dirt's shores are just geological phenomena that appear in the wet season. Those who have stumbled across these traps know the dangerous reality.

Few know much about palpares, an enormous insect whose plated, hulking abdomen takes up most of its size. They seem to be solitary ambush hunters that hibernate during the dry season, then awaken during the Flood to create their enormous pit traps. Estos traps capture prey of all sizes, even the occasional herd of migrating aurochs, as they wait buried in the center. Though usually very patient, when disturbed, a palpares can move through its native sandy soil surprisingly quick, greeting intruders who enter its domain with its shovellike head and vicious pincers.

Life Stages

Research suggests palpares aren't yet in its final form of life, as large caverns on the shores have been discovered to hold traces of chitin and the rotting remains of palpares partially transformed. Though nobody has encountered an adult and lived to tell the tale, rumors abound that the fully fledged insect form resembles Rovagug. Communities are quick to locate and dispose of any pupae they find in large, sand-encrusted mounds in the dirt. Some towns hold large barbecues to harvest tons of "mud bacon."

Spite-Screamer.publicNotes:
Wights are intelligent undead spawned through inescapable cycles of spite. Este spite might come from their own malevolent will in life, or can be instilled by necromantic rituals, typically involving the desecration of burial sites. Wights usually haunt burial grounds, catacombs, or other places of the dead. Their hunger is targeted toward the living—those whose pumping hearts and ruddy warmth inspire visceral hatred.

As many types of wights exist as types of people from which they might be created. Hulking brutes, skittering sneaks, and cunning tinkers all make for different wights with different niches to fill. The environment, too, plays a part in determining a wight's special abilities and defenses. Frost wights, for instance, can be found in parts of the world where exposure is a common end and the resentment of being left alone in the wild is a common source of spite. Durable and sustained by void energy, wights can last in harsh environments without decaying the way some lesser undead do.

A single wight can wreak significant havoc if it is compelled to rise from its tomb. Because criaturas slain under a wight's curse can become wights as well, all it takes is a single wight and a handful of unlucky graveyard visitors to create a veritable horde of these undead. Thus, canny priests and adventurers know that the best solution to a wight problem is swift and total eradication. Care must be taken, though, to destroy wight spawn before attempting to destroy the parent wight, for spawn without a maestro gain the ability to create spawn of their own.

Stormblood Tiger.publicNotes:
Whereas most werecreatures follow el monthly rhythms de el full moon, el stormblood tiger's change es connected a el floods brought by annual rainfall. In parts de el world where flooding o heavy rains son both regular y predictable, such as during el Deluge en Belkzen, these lycanthropes stalk el land hunting for prey. Every night after el floods begin, un stormblood tiger es forced into su hybrid form until sun rises o el waters recede, usually 2–3 meses later. El remainder de el ano, stormblood tigers walk undetected among el population, often mistaken for hunters o scouts.

Sought Out

Because de el stormblood tiger's fearsome reputation y powerful abilities, some foolhardy orc warriors view becoming un stormblood tiger as un path a greatness—un blessing instead de un curse. In su minds, ello's more important a tienen este power at hand during times de conflict than worry about disrupting peace during el Flood Truce. Wiser voices argue que too many stormblood tigers roaming about during el Flood Truce risks ending el accord altogether.

Trighouls were originally created over a thousand years ago by fleshwarpers aligned with the Whispering Tyrant, giving them to raiders as armas. While the use of trighouls is now regarded with shame and disgust, some still take advantage of the criaturas to lure enemies to their deaths using the corpses of their slain comrades.

Puppetmaster Serum

The elixir transforms the drinker's limb into a tentacle that can temporarily animate the dead. One must take great care when CRAFTING the serum, as incorrectly mixed batches have been known to dissolve organs from within, cause permanent paralysis, and grow tentacles in unwanted places.

Troll.name: Trol
Troll.publicNotes:
Forest trolls are gangly giants who stalk the fringes of civilization. They rely on their incredible strength to overpower foes with their vicious claws and toothy maws. Estos trolls stand anywhere from 12 to 16 pies tall, though they prefer to hunch for comfort and to lull foes into a false sense of security. Trolls are truly criaturas of the forest, deeply linked in flesh and blood to the verdant habitats they consider their territory. In fact, when a forest troll is killed, their flesh turns into blackened lumps of charcoal, often still glowing with coals. Despite that, these criaturas roam farther and wider than most of their kin, to the extent that they're the first criaturas a common person thinks of when they hear the word "troll."

Slavering, cruel, invincible brutes: this is the villager's stock description for the dread monsters known as trolls. The roots of these stories are undoubtedly true. Trolls' flesh endlessly regrows, going so far as to sprout aberrant limbs or additional heads if not pruned, and a bottomless hunger is required to feed such unfettered growth. Even in the process of glutting themselves, however, trolls find opportunities to taunt their prey and inflict petty cruelties.

A troll's ability to survive is so strong that they believe even the smallest scrap of flesh will slowly regenerate into a new form, suffering as all the powers of the land are gathered to revive them. Despite the pain, trolls speak of this unassailable vitality as a blessing from their creator. Few trolls have heard the laughter of demons who claim that creator cursed the trolls and cast them down from lofty heights, binding them so they could never rise again.

Trolls prefer to remain solitary, keeping every scrap of food for themselves. In rare instances, an old and powerful troll comes to lead groups of trolls. Such warleaders possess enough cunning to lead their hordes in devastating raids and massacres, and their presence permanently alters the surrounding ecosystem. Este link to their environment is an often misunderstood aspect of trollkind, and grows more acute with a troll's age and power. That's not to say trolls are valorous protectors of NATURE. They're vicious and territorial, and will blight their own territory forever if it means more to eat for a day.

War Pig.publicNotes:
While not native to Belkzen, these swine instead descended from livestock raided and re-homed millennia ago during orc raids. Generations of selective breeding favored larger animals suited to Belkzen's harsh environment and fearsome predators, resulting in the modern war pig. During the flood season, these pigs gorge and grow fat, gradually consuming their reserves to become leaner and meaner during the rest of the year.

Arguably domesticated, war pigs rarely remain in captivity for more than a few generations. Most orcs loathe the notion of their swine becoming too tame, instead releasing part of their herd every year to grow fierce before recapturing them seasons later. The downside is that these feral swine associate humanoids with food. rogue war pigs sometimes form roving gangs that uproot fields, run amok, and even knock over trade caravans to eat rations (and the occasional merchant).

The "war" in war pigs comes from their use as mounts. With the right motivation, a war pig is a porcine juggernaut able to carry a fully armored orc into combat. Without discipline, care, and treats, that same pig can become 600 pounds of willful chaos that's as likely to trample foes as it is to flee combat, find a mud puddle, and crush its rider after flopping down to vigorously wallow.

Wight Spell Sniper.name: Wight Spell Sniper
Wight Spell Sniper.hpDetails: fueled by spite, curación de vacío
Wight Spell Sniper.publicNotes:
Wights are intelligent undead spawned through inescapable cycles of spite. Este spite might come from their own malevolent will in life, or can be instilled by necromantic rituals, typically involving the desecration of burial sites. Wights usually haunt burial grounds, catacombs, or other places of the dead. Their hunger is targeted toward the living—those whose pumping hearts and ruddy warmth inspire visceral hatred.

As many types of wights exist as types of people from which they might be created. Hulking brutes, skittering sneaks, and cunning tinkers all make for different wights with different niches to fill. The environment, too, plays a part in determining a wight's special abilities and defenses. Frost wights, for instance, can be found in parts of the world where exposure is a common end and the resentment of being left alone in the wild is a common source of spite. Durable and sustained by void energy, wights can last in harsh environments without decaying the way some lesser undead do.

A single wight can wreak significant havoc if it is compelled to rise from its tomb. Because criaturas slain under a wight's curse can become wights as well, all it takes is a single wight and a handful of unlucky graveyard visitors to create a veritable horde of these undead. Thus, canny priests and adventurers know that the best solution to a wight problem is swift and total eradication. Care must be taken, though, to destroy wight spawn before attempting to destroy the parent wight, for spawn without a maestro gain the ability to create spawn of their own.

Yagrekash.name: Yagrekash
Yagrekash.publicNotes:
Einherjar are mighty warriors chosen by valkyries from the ranks of those slain in terrible and legendario battles. Forged from the souls of the greatest warriors, the implacable einherjar serve as the pies soldiers of pantheons, skilled in handto-hand combat and slaying giants.

Einherjar often come from warrior cultures, including Ulfen vikings (like the einherji represented in this entry), particularly fierce pirates from the Shackles, and even Osirian conquerors. They can be chosen from wherever war and might hold sway; many deities who hold the call of battle and the pursuit of physical power more sacred than concepts of good and evil might count einherjar warriors and valkyrie choosers of the slain among their chosen servitors. For example, Gorum, Besmara, and Sekhmet have all elevated fallen worshippers as einherjar. Einherjar dedicated to different deities often wield armas or possess varying cosmetic appearances based on their deity's preferred arma and their place of death; however, they're universally stalwart, implacable, and efficiently deadly. Einherjar with two-handed armas or who arise from other backgrounds often have different abilities in place of Jotun Slayer and Instant REPAIR.
